title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
author: Anthropic
takes: Context rot and an attention budget: more tokens, worse recall. Three tools for long work - compaction (risks losing what matters later), structured notes outside the window (NOTES.md), sub-agents that return 1-2 thousand token summaries; load knowledge just in time by reference.

title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
author: Anthropic
takes: Compaction alone was not enough: each fresh session gets up to speed from a progress file, the git log and a feature list, works one item, commits and writes its progress. Whether specialised agents beat one general agent is left open.

title: Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions
author: Anthropic
takes: Teammates message each other directly, not only through the lead; 3-5 teammates; each starts from project context and a spawn prompt, never the lead's history; in-process teammates are not restored on resume; for routine or sequential work one session is cheaper.

title: Claude Code agent memory frontmatter
author: shanraisshan
takes: Since v2.1.33 a subagent can keep its own MEMORY.md (project scope in .claude/agent-memory/NAME/), its first 200 lines put in its prompt each time: the field writes expertise down per role rather than keeping it in a session; each role's memory is siloed from the others.

title: Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working
author: Walden Yan (Cognition)
takes: A narrower class works: writes stay single-threaded and extra agents contribute intelligence, not actions. Consulting a 'smart friend' works best by sharing a fork of the asker's full context; unstructured swarms of negotiating agents are a distraction.

title: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Architectures
author: Will Fu-Hinthorn (LangChain)
takes: A supervisor that relays every message plays telephone: it scored lower and spent more tokens than agents handing off directly; removing routing chatter from the workers' context closed much of the gap.

title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
author: Zhang et al.
takes: Knowledge kept by rewriting one summary erodes (context collapse) and drifts toward the terse (brevity bias); itemised, incremental additions to a playbook keep the detail. ICLR 2026.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
author: Cemri et al.
takes: 1600+ traces, 14 failure modes in three groups: system design, misalignment between agents (lost context, ignored input, withheld information), task verification. Gains from multi-agent systems are often minimal. NeurIPS 2025.

title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
author: Hong, Troynikov, Huber (Chroma)
takes: Models do worse as input grows, even on simple tasks and well below the window's size; focused inputs beat full ones.

title: Exploring Advanced LLM Multi-Agent Systems Based on Blackboard Architecture
author: Han and Zhang
takes: Agents share one blackboard instead of private memories; a control unit picks who acts from what is on it. With 2510.01285 (agents volunteer for requests posted to the board): routing by a shared record, not by a central relay.

title: Sleep-time Compute
author: Letta
takes: Stateful agents keep editable memory blocks; a separate agent rewrites them between tasks into clean, concise learned context, so the working agent need not re-derive it.

title: Diátaxis: a systematic approach to technical documentation
author: Daniele Procida
takes: Four kinds by the reader's need - tutorial, how-to, reference, explanation - never mixed on one page. Reference is neutral and looked up: in a tad base, the tables; how-to is the named records and briefs; explanation is decisions, concepts and the occasional essay.

title: The /llms.txt file
author: Jeremy Howard
takes: One Markdown file at a fixed path: a title, a one-line summary, then sections of links with a note each, and an Optional section an agent may skip when short of context. A router, not the content.

title: AGENTS.md
author: agents.md
takes: A README for agents; the nearest AGENTS.md to the file being edited wins. The one file every agent already looks for - the place for a base's single entry.

title: Documenting Architecture Decisions
author: Michael Nygard
takes: One significant decision per record, numbered and never reused; a reversed decision is kept, marked superseded, pointing at what replaced it. docs' decisions table is this, with rejected beside it.

title: MADR: Markdown Architectural Decision Records 4.0
author: MADR project
takes: Adds considered options with pros and cons and a status that says superseded by which. What docs' decisions already keep as decision, why, rejected.

title: Data Package (Frictionless Data)
author: Frictionless Data
takes: datapackage.json at the top is the descriptor and index of the data's resources, each with a stable name and a schema. tables.toml follows its Table Schema; tad statements is the same kind of index for questions.

title: Docs as Code
author: Write the Docs
takes: Documentation in plain text, in git, reviewed and tested like code. What every tad base already is.

title: Evergreen notes
author: Andy Matuschak
takes: Atomic, concept-oriented, densely linked notes whose titles work like APIs; outline notes link many notes. One row is one such note; a checked link is the dense link; a query is the outline note.

title: Johnny.Decimal
author: Johnny Noble
takes: A fixed small index - no more than ten at each level - kept as a first-class record of every id. A base's entry should be that small.

title: The PARA Method
author: Tiago Forte
takes: Organise by actionability: projects, areas, resources, archives. In a base, what is actionable is read off status (open backlog), not filed by folder.

title: Help:Statements (Wikidata)

title: Help:Infobox (Wikipedia)

takes: A fixed-format summary of facts beside the prose that explains them; the facts must stand in the prose with citations too. Tables for facts, prose for reasons.

title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills

takes: Three levels: a name and one line always loaded, the body when relevant, linked files only when needed; scripts run without being read. The shape of a base's entry: AGENTS.md, tad statements, a query's rows, one row.

title: pmaports device-google-blueline deviceinfo (Pixel 3, booted on stock ABL)
author: postmarketOS
takes: A working recipe on a sibling Pixel ABL: base 0, kernel 0x8000, ramdisk 0x1000000, second 0x0, tags 0x100, page 4096, dtb appended, cmdline console=ttyMSM0,115200 only, no os_version.

title: Android Bootloader and Linux Internal based on Nokia 8 (NB1): DT loading in ABL
author: Inoki
takes: On an MSM8998 phone ABL's DeviceTreeAppended scans every dtb appended to the kernel and DeviceTreeCompatible picks the best by qcom,msm-id, qcom,board-id, qcom,pmic-id; the ABL, not the kernel, chooses and patches the dt.

title: Android: Use multiple DTs (device tree overlays in the bootloader)
author: AOSP
takes: The bootloader loads the SoC dtb, identifies the board, loads the matching dtbo overlay from the dtbo partition and merges them before starting the kernel: a failed merge is a bootloader refusal.

title: Android SE: Pixel 2 bootloader loop, fastboot boot of TWRP walleye gives Load Error
author: Joachim
takes: A known-good walleye TWRP image also gets 'Failed to load/authenticate boot image: Load Error' from fastboot boot when the phone's slot state is odd: the message is not proof the image is bad.

title: XDA: Troubles reinstalling TWRP [Failed to load/authenticate boot image: Load Error]
